records.label: II.4

phenotypes.text: bilateral small cystic lesions of basal ganglia

quotes: The index case (II.4 Table 1 and Fig. 1A), a 34 years old man, was admitted in the emergency ward for a sudden left hemiparesis. He had a history of a nonsevere mental retardation, and was admitted 2 years before in psychiatry unit for an acute psychotic episode followed by generalized seizures.
The clinical status of the patient progressively worsened over a 20 years period with a severe neuropsychological deterioration and a spastic tetraplegia. He died in 2011, no autopsy was performed.

Arteriography was normal as well as electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), Doppler ultrasound, and cardiac echocardiography. Among biological analysis, a dipstick urine test for sulfites (MQuant, VWR®) was positive.

records.label: II.5

phenotypes.text: basal ganglia cystic lesions (deep cavitating state)

records.segregation: c.670dupA inherited from asymptomatic mother; variants on different alleles; asymptomatic sibs carried neither
quotes: In 2014, one of his brother (II.5, Table 1 and Fig. 1A) was admitted in the intensive care for a sudden coma with cardiovascular collapse. He was a 58 years old man with a history of diabetes mellitus and had lived an active professional life.
The urine sulfite test was also positive. The patient progressively recovered but presented with a neuropsychological deterioration (BREF: 14/18, MMSE: 22/30).

two rare variants were found in the NIT1 gene (Nitrilase‐like protein 1, NM_005600): an heterozygous c.457G > A;p.Gly153Arg variation and an heterozygous c.670dupA;p.Thr224Asnfs*41 variation (Fig. 1B–C).

records.label: II.7
records.segregation: c.670dupA inherited from asymptomatic mother; asymptomatic sibs carried neither variant
quotes: A third brother of the family was in a psychiatric institution for a schizophrenia diagnosed 40 years ago (II.7). His clinical examination was normal, but the CT scan and the MRI (3 T) found the same brain lesions together with a positive urine sulfite test.
An inherited recessive disorder was suspected and an exome study was performed on individuals II.7 and II.5 DNA.

records.label: 3 affected siblings

phenotypes.text: numerous massively dilated basal ganglia perivascular spaces

quotes: The first identified patients were 3 siblings, compound heterozygous for the NIT1 c.727C>T; (p.Arg243Trp) variant and the NIT1 c.198_199del; p.(Ala68∗) variant.

Patients presented in mid-adulthood with movement disorders. All patients had striking abnormalities on brain magnetic resonance imaging, with numerous and massively dilated basal ganglia perivascular spaces.

notes.statement: Rutten et al. (2024) reported that 3 of 7 patients with NIT1-related small vessel disease had nonlobar intracerebral hemorrhage between ages 45 and 60 years, which was fatal in 2. Brain autopsy showed large electron-dense deposits in the vessel walls of small and medium-sized cerebral arteries.
quotes: Three patients had non-lobar intracerebral hemorrhage between age 45 and 60, which was fatal in 2 cases.
Brain autopsy revealed large electron-dense deposits in the vessel walls of small and medium sized cerebral arteries.

notes.statement: Rutten et al. (2024) found that western blotting of patient fibroblasts showed absence of NIT1 protein, and metabolic analysis of urine confirmed loss of NIT1 enzymatic function, consistent with loss-of-function variants.
quotes: Western blotting on patient fibroblasts showed absence of NIT1 protein, and metabolic analysis in urine confirmed loss of NIT1 enzymatic function.

notes.statement: Rutten et al. (2024) described NIT1-small vessel disease as a novel autosomal recessive cerebral small vessel disease characterized by a triad of movement disorders, massively dilated basal ganglia perivascular spaces, and intracerebral hemorrhage.
quotes: NIT1-small vessel disease is a novel, autosomal recessively inherited cerebral small vessel disease characterized by a triad of movement disorders, massively dilated basal ganglia perivascular spaces, and intracerebral hemorrhage.

notes.statement: Rendu et al. (2019) showed that the c.457G>A variant, which affects the last nucleotide of exon 4 of NIT1, disrupted splicing in transcripts from patient skin. NIT1 protein could not be detected by Western blot in the patient's fibroblasts. Molecular cloning showed that the two variants were on different alleles.
quotes: It is also located on the last nucleotide of exon 4 and predicted to affect the splicing of NIT1 mRNA, which was next demonstrated by sequencing of the NIT1 transcript extracted from a skin biopsy of patient II.5 (data not shown).
Accordingly, the level of Nit1 protein was undetectable by western blot in fibroblasts from patient II.5 (Fig. 1D).
molecular cloning of a PCR fragment encompassing both variations from patient II.5 showed that they were initially present on different alleles of the gene (not shown).

notes.statement: Rendu et al. (2019) found a deaminated glutathione (dGSH) derivative by GC/MS in the urine of the affected brothers but not in unaffected sibs or the mother. Its mass spectrum resembled the compound seen in Nit1-knockout mice, and the authors suggested that dGSH probably caused the positive urine sulfite test. Patient fibroblasts showed a twofold increase in mitochondrial MnSOD activity, while cytoplasmic Cu/Zn SOD activity was unchanged.
quotes: The same peaks were observed in urine of his brothers (II.5 and II.7) but were undetectable in the other siblings tested and the mother.
The loss of function of the gene led to the accumulation of dGSH, which was detected in the urine of patients, and probably responsible for the positive urine sulfite test.
The cytoplasmic SOD (Cu/Zn SOD) activity was not changed, whilst the activity of the mitochondrial SOD (MnSOD) showed a twofold increase as compared to control samples

notes.statement: Rendu et al. (2019) described a novel autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by NIT1 mutations. It combines neurologic signs, cavitating (cystic) lesions of the basal ganglia, and a positive urine sulfite test. The authors suggested the sulfite test could be used to screen psychiatric patients for the disease.
quotes: Overall, we described here a novel autosomal recessive metabolic disorder due to mutations in the NIT1 gene which associates neurological signs, basal ganglia lesions as well as positive urine sulfite test, the latter being easily used to screen for the disease in cohorts of psychiatric patients.

notes.statement: Rendu et al. (2019) noted that, before this report, the only conditions known to combine brain damage with a positive urinary sulfite test were sulfite oxidase deficiency and molybdenum cofactor deficiency. Both were excluded in this family.
quotes: To date, the only known pathologies showing brain damage together with a positive urinary sulfite test are sulfite oxidase deficiency and molybdenum cofactor deficiency.12, 13 These pathologies were excluded and we identify here a novel nosological entity.
